children.approach: Lemma: the Hessian of d^beta N(h) has entries M_ij = c_{beta+e_i+e_j}, the RAW coefficients, since d^gamma((c_gamma/gamma!)x^gamma) = c_gamma. Consequence: the 2x2-minor necessary condition (RLC) is log-concavity of the RAW coefficients, and the same inequality on normalized coefficients is strictly weaker (factorial ratio alpha_i alpha_j / ((alpha_i+1)(alpha_j+1)) < 1). Verified symbolically over all beta at ell=3, d=4.

Theorem: if c_gamma = prod_t f_t(gamma_t) with each f_t log-concave with interval support (PF_2), then N(h) is Lorentzian. Mechanism: M = P uu^T - (nonneg diagonal), so lambda_2 <= lambda_2(rank-one PSD) = 0 by Weyl; the four cases |Z|=0,1,2,>=3 of zero-indices Z={k: f_k(beta_k)=0} are handled separately (|Z|=1 gives an arrow matrix of rank <=2 with negative 2x2 determinant). (L2) proved directly by the box-slice exchange axiom. Controls: 1105 random product-form instances, 0 failures; NEGATIVE control, 3604 of 5573 non-log-concave product forms FAIL (L3), so the hypothesis is load-bearing.

Corollary: for m=1 the cylindric horizontal-strip condition reads nu_1 <= rho_1 < nu_1 + n, so K^c_alpha = prod_t 1_{[0,n-1]}(alpha_t) exactly; 1_{[0,n-1]} is PF_2, so product-form applies. Settles every one-bead cylindric shape at every level n and every ell. Contains a two-line proof that e_d is Lorentzian (n=2: M = J_S - I_S, lambda_2 = -1). Characterisation checked against the chain recursion: 165/165 for 2<=n<=7, d<=n, ell<=5. The family WINDS, so this is not a restatement of the ordinary case.

Proposition: at ell=2 the constraints on the single intermediate cylindric shape kappa DECOUPLE -- kappa_i in [max(mu_i, lam_{i-1}+1), min(lam_i, mu_{i+1}-1)], one independent interval per bead, each involving only the fixed data mu,lam. The tuple is automatically a cylindric shape (kappa_i <= mu_{i+1}-1 < mu_{i+1} <= kappa_{i+1}; wrap from mu_{m+1}=mu_1+n). Hence sum_a k_a z^a is a product of interval indicators. Checked against BOTH the chain recursion and brute-force enumeration of intermediate shapes: 3224/3224 shapes for 2<=n<=7, 1<=m<=n, d<=10.

Lemma (classically Hoggar, but proved here from scratch so as not to rest on an uncited source): PF_2 = log-concave with interval support is closed under convolution. Proof: T(f*g) = T(f)T(g) on bi-infinite Toeplitz matrices, and by Cauchy-Binet every 2x2 minor of a product is a finite sum of products of pairs of 2x2 minors; nonnegativity of all 2x2 Toeplitz minors is verified directly for an interval indicator (the anti-diagonal index pair {r,s} is strictly more spread than {p,q} at equal sum, so f(r)f(s)=1 forces f(p)f(q)=1) and implies log-concavity (rows {i,i+1}, cols {k,k+1}). Controls: 3e5 random interval-indicator minors, 0 negative; 44409 random PF_2 convolution pairs, 0 failures.

Theorem: N(s^c_{lambda/mu}(x_1,x_2)) is Lorentzian for EVERY cylindric skew shape, every level n, every m. From ell2-decoupling + pf2-convolution the sequence k_a = K^c_{(a,d-a)} is log-concave with interval support; (L2) is then the interval property and (L3) is det[[k_{a+2},k_{a+1}],[k_{a+1},k_a]] = k_a k_{a+2} - k_{a+1}^2 <= 0 via raw-hessian-lemma.

Q256 falsifier, run BEFORE attempting the proof as the brief required. 3647 instances (2<=n<=6, 1<=m<=n, d<=9, 2<=ell<=6), 1899 winding (52.1%): ZERO failures of (L2), of exact (L3), or of (RLC) on raw coefficients. A 517-instance subsweep (228 winding, 44.1%) also found 0 failures of the normalized (RLC). All (L3) decisions exact: integer characteristic polynomial by Faddeev-LeVerrier over Q plus Descartes' rule (exact for real-rooted polynomials), never float eigenvalues. Census of where (L3) is tight, to constrain any future proof. Among the 2238 nonzero Hessians from WINDING instances with m>=2: lambda_2 = 0 EXACTLY in 1637 (73.1%), lambda_2 < 0 in 601 (26.9%). So the conjecture, if true, sits on the boundary of the Lorentzian cone about three times in four -- no argument with slack can work. Separately, the product-form mechanism (off-diagonal part of M rank one, i.e. M_ij M_kl = M_il M_kj for distinct i,j,k,l) holds in 1280/1658 Hessians with ell>=4 (77.2%) and fails in 22.8%.

children.approach: ATTEMPT: reduce to the ordinary case via Postnikov's toric Schur theorem, which in its range of validity expands s^c in Schur functions with nonnegative Gromov-Witten coefficients, then apply HMMS Thm 3 (normalized Schur polynomials are Lorentzian).

children.approach: THE OPEN REGIME, stated precisely: ell >= 3 AND m >= 2. The reason the ell=2 proof does not generalise is structural, not technical: the horizontal-strip condition kappa^{t+1}_i < kappa^t_{i+1} makes bead i at time t+1 depend on bead i+1 at time t, so consecutive INTERIOR layers couple and the coefficient sequence stops being a convolution of independent interval indicators. The coupling is absent at ell=2 because there is only one interior layer, and absent at m=1 because i+1 = i. Then comparable-mlr gives P(u,.) <=_lr P(u',.), which is (B).

Proposition (ALL m): k(a,b)=k(b,a)= sum over the box-slice {nu in Box(mu): S_nu=|mu|+b} of f_nu(a), where Box(mu)=prod_i [mu_i,mu_{i+1}-1] and f_nu = conv_i 1_{[L_i(nu)-nu_i, R_i(nu)-nu_i]}, L_i=max(nu_i,lam_{i-1}+1), R_i=min(nu_{i+1}-1,lam_i). Proof: the mu-<nu constraints decouple per bead (so the admissible nu are exactly a BOX), and given nu the nu-<kappa-<lam constraints decouple per bead too; cylindricity is automatic both times. Each f_nu is PF2 by ell2-decoupling + pf2-convolution. CONSEQUENCE: (A) is not a statement about a three-step chain -- it is 'a sum of PF2 sequences over one slice of a box is log-concave', a ONE-PARAMETER statement. Verified: reproduces k exactly on 227/227 instances, and the underlying K^c code cross-checked against an independent chain enumeration 647/647.

Proposition (m=2): the slice is 1-dimensional (t=nu_1), and (A) becomes EXACTLY G(s)=sum_{i+j=s}(Phi(i)-Psi(j)+1)_+ over i in [lam_2-n+1, lam_1], j in [lam_1+1, lam_2], with Phi(i)=min(i,u-1-i,T_+) concave and Psi(j)=max(u-j,j-n+1,T_-) convex, BOTH 1-LIPSCHITZ (each is a min/max of three affine functions of slope +1,-1,0). Theorem (m=2): the four endpoint functions a_t=max(t,A), b_t=min(u-1-t,B), c_t=max(u-t,C), d_t=min(t+n-1,D) (A=lam_2-n+1, B=lam_1, C=B+1, D=lam_2) share only TWO breakpoints, tau_1=A=D-n+1 (for a,d) and tau_2=u-1-B=u-C (for b,c). So the t-range meets at most four cells, and G=G_I+G_II+G_III+G_IV with EACH summand PF2, by two different proved mechanisms. Regions I,III: one of the two intervals is CONSTANT in t, so G_I = 1_{[A,B]} * w_I with w_I(x)=(p_1-max(u-x,x-n+1,p_0)+1)_+ the positive part of a concave function, hence PF2, and pf2-convolution finishes (symmetrically for III). Regions II,IV: a_t+c_t and b_t+d_t are both CONSTANT, so every trapezoid has the same support and G_R(s)=rho_R(H(s)) with H(s)=min(s-ell+1,h-s+1) concave and rho_R(v)=sum_t min(v,n_t,m_t)_+ concave nondecreasing -- hence G_R is CONCAVE on its support, hence PF2. Verified: the four closed forms are exact (I 1363/1363, II 2988/2988, III 1363/1363, IV 579/579) and the decomposition identity holds on 2655/2655 slices.

Lemma 1: a symmetric 3x3 M with nonnegative entries satisfying (A) M_ij^2>=M_ii M_jj and (B) M_ik M_kj >= M_ij M_kk has at most one positive eigenvalue. Proof: the identity det M = P+2t-x-y-z with xyz=P t^2 (P=prod diag, t=prod offdiag, x=M_11 M_23^2 etc); (B) multiplied through gives exactly x,y,z <= t, so for t>0 det M = t*g(x/t,y/t,z/t) with g(xi,eta,zeta)=xi*eta*zeta-xi-eta-zeta+2 MULTILINEAR, hence minimised at a vertex of [0,1]^3 where it takes values 2,1,0,0. Lemma 2: if f <=_lr f', g <=_lr g' and all four are PF2, then f*g <=_lr f'*g'. Proof: reduce by transitivity to one factor at a time; then for v<v', S := (f*g)(v)(f'*g)(v') - (f*g)(v')(f'*g)(v) = sum_{w,w'} f(w)f'(w') Delta(w,w') with Delta antisymmetric, so 2S = sum [f(w)f'(w')-f(w')f'(w)] Delta(w,w'); the first bracket is >=0 for w<w' by f<=_lr f', and Delta(w,w') = g(p)g(p'+delta)-g(p+delta)g(p') >= 0 for p>p' by PF2 of g. Both brackets are antisymmetric and sign-matched, so every term is >=0.
